items.summary: FSY says Caiden is approved to preregister for the summer 2027 conference, with timing depending on his stake's cycle.
items.action: Check your stake's FSY cycle and preregister
items.body:
Dear Caiden,

You are invited to attend a For the Strength of Youth (FSY) conference in summer 2027. You already have your bishopric's approval to preregister.

If your stake is on-cycle this year, you can preregister now. If your stake is off-cycle, preregistration opens February 15, 2027.

Preregistration lets you choose preferred sessions and request to be at a session with others using a session link. Use the FSY Dashboard to preregister, find session updates, and edit your registration information.

items.subject: Give it everything you've got
items.summary: Sister Heintzelman shares her busy final weeks as a missionary in Brownsville and offers homecoming details on request.
items.body:
Apparently when you try to avoid talking or thinking about your mission ending, everyone else gets the exact opposite idea. Every member and missionary that I know has been asking me about going home and my last meals.

Speaking of which we had a very busy week. A sweet talk with Hermana Pineda, a Spanish exchange in La Joya where the friend we taught, Cesar, got baptized on Sunday, and a great lesson with Gabriel, Neydy, and two of their kids.

Hardest point of this week was when our dear friend Maria decided she would no longer come to church or be baptized. I am so grateful to have been part of her story.

All in all this week has been full of love, laughter, and growth. I'm giving it everything I've got. God can make the most beautiful garden out of your worst desert. Trust Him, His plan and timing.

May God be with you all til we meet again.

- Sister Heintzelman

Also if you want the information for my arrival and my homecoming, go ahead and reach out!

items.subject: Great and dreadful day pt2
items.summary: Brysen writes from Africa that he stays in the same area with his companion but is moving apartments.
items.body:
Hey everyone hows life going? The work of the Lord is still booming for me down here in Africa.

For now, let's talk about transfers. I am staying in the same area with the same companion, which I am very much not mad at all about. I am moving apartments. My current one is the celestial apartment, with minimal cockroaches and no mice. My next home is an apartment that the church just bought, so who knows what it's gonna be like.

Spiritual thought: On Tuesday we heard a devotional from Elder Morrison of the 70. He talked about how if we are not actively working to grow or protect our testimonies, the devil will begin to break them. As important as spiritual experiences are, it's almost more important what happens after.

Love yall and have a great week!

items.subject: Yup Thats Mamalodi
items.summary: Elder Nelson shares a week in Mamelodi with zone leader exchanges, eight investigators at church, and a zoo trip.
items.body:
Matthew 10:38, 39.

This week Wednesday we went on zone leader exchanges. It was priceless to see our beloved zone leader walk through Mamelodi. We went to a lesson in an informal settlement. When we showed up to meet the guy (Sam), the water turned on. He said it was a miracle and we were sent from God.

This week was an amazing week for sharing the gospel. We had 8 investigators show up to church, one of which was Sam. Sam said next week he would bring his family to church.

Going to the zoo with my district!!

Love yall,
Elder Nelson

items.subject: Transfer 3!!
items.summary: McKay reports a new area in Montana, a new companion, and a person he invited to baptism.
items.body:
Wassup gang, so sorry its been a few weeks since my last email. Transfers happened. But before that, 2 days before transfers, Elder Langston and I put someone on date! We visited a woman named Sue, had a good lesson, then went back and invited her to be baptized. She said she was just thinking the same thing, and accepted.

Then I got the news I'm going to the west side, to the Bitterroot YSA area. My new companion is Elder Welch and we are the Bitterroot Zone Leaders. We live with 2 other elders in a trailer house, super messy, but we have been cleaning it out. I love it here and I love you all!

Thanks to the people who sent me the most elite Halloween packages and snacks!

New address: [removed]

items.subject: Trust
items.summary: Elder Adamson writes from the ER about a torn shoulder and shares thoughts on trusting God's plan.
items.body:
Why do bad things happen to us? Why is there evil in this world? Why do we have to feel pain?

Happy birthday to my boy Max Barton! So bad news fans, I am writing this from the ER. I tore my shoulder. Not even the most tragic thing that happened this last week. BYU lost to Utah.

Now I do not know what will happen with my shoulder. It could be another torn labrum which means surgery. But I have complete confidence in Nephi's words in 1 Nephi 3:7. No matter what happens, serving a mission is my commandment. Expect miracles friends and family. Prayers would be much appreciated.

For overcoming adversity, I invite you to listen to Jon Huntsman's BYU devotional: God Did Not Put Us Here to Fail.

Love you all,
Elder Adamson
